protected_thesis: BayesBreak is the method developed in Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Segmentation with Irregular Designs, Multi-Sequence Hierarchies, and Grouped/Latent-Group Designs. For supported observation models, family-specific segment marginal likelihoods and posterior moments enter common sum-product recursions for posterior quantities and a separate max-sum recursion with backtracking for the joint MAP partition. The implementation must preserve irregular-design priors, common and group-specific changepoints across multiple sequences, known groups, and the finite latent-group criterion stated in the manuscript.
do_not_change: Do not change the manuscript title or replace generalized hierarchical Bayesian segmentation as the main scientific narrative without explicit author approval.
Do not overwrite populated archived numerical results; a corrected computation receives a new result ID and an explicit parent-result link.
Do not interpret the finite latent-group criterion as a normalized finite-mixture likelihood.
Do not use marginal changepoint modes as the joint MAP partition.
Do not treat agreement with BayesBreak MAP changepoints as accuracy against independent truth.
Do not use RES-BB-CMP-002 or RES-BB-RD-007Q in comparator or posterior-predictive conclusions.
Do not describe the method with vague branding; use the defined probability model, prior, recursion, optimization objective, metric, or numerical criterion.

experiments.competing: Agreement is limited to hand-picked priors or benign support.

definition_of_done: The exact title and generalized hierarchical Bayesian segmentation narrative remain unchanged across the book, main paper, executive summary, code handoff, and presentation handoffs.
Exact finite-case dynamic-programming properties match exhaustive enumeration under seeded tests.
Posterior prediction is family-specific and out-of-range coordinates follow an explicit recorded policy.
Comparator axes, reference type, matching rule, and tuning budget are validated before metric computation.
Every corrected result has a new ID, a parent link, and data, configuration, code, and environment hashes; archived populated values remain unchanged.
Book appendix, task registry, figures, tables, and metadata pass synchronization checks.
Every unresolved proof, test, computation, annotation, or release decision is stated directly rather than represented as complete.
non_goals: No normalized latent-mixture model is implemented in this work program.
No online changepoint detector, slope-change model, or graph segmentation method is introduced.
No archived result is silently corrected in place.
No fixed package version, compute budget, or completion date is invented before version and resource profiling are resolved.
No slide deck is generated by this manuscript workflow.

test_matrix.acceptance: No populated archived value changes; invalid historical calculations cannot re-enter excluded conclusions.

logging_and_provenance: Record result_id and parent_result_id before writing a corrected result.
Record data, configuration, code, and environment hashes for every new run.
Store the coordinate axis, observation family, prior, split, extrapolation policy, metric version, and tuning budget with each relevant result.
Report executed, valid for the stated interpretation, excluded from a named analysis, and planned as separate fields.
Reject absolute author-local paths in release records.
resource_expectations: Profile the one test unresolved under the Phase 6 per-test cap before setting time or memory budgets.
Account explicitly for the O(n^2) segment-score table and O(k_max n^2) worst-case partition recursions.
Measure sequence count, candidate count, observation family, nonconjugate method, repetitions, and comparator tuning as separate resource drivers.
Produce pilot-based CPU, memory, storage, and wall-time estimates before the expanded experiment grid; the current archive does not support a defensible fixed estimate.

failure_states.condition: Nonfinite or dimensionally inconsistent segment scores.
failure_states.required_behavior: Stop before partition inference and emit the offending family, segment coordinates, and configuration hash.

failure_states.condition: Comparator prediction and reference axes differ.
failure_states.required_behavior: Reject metric computation; preserve the attempted run only as a diagnostic record.

failure_states.condition: Posterior prediction requested for an unsupported family or coordinate outside support.
failure_states.required_behavior: Raise an explicit error unless a named, recorded extrapolation rule is selected.

failure_states.condition: Latent-group objective is nonmonotone beyond tolerance or returned objective differs from the final trace value.
failure_states.required_behavior: Mark the restart invalid and do not select it as the optimum.

failure_states.condition: A required test exceeds its profiled bound.
failure_states.required_behavior: Report unresolved with owner, environment, seed, and profile; do not count it as a pass.

failure_states.condition: A corrected result lacks a parent link or required hashes.
failure_states.required_behavior: Reject release of the result and retain the archived parent unchanged.
